SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT

S. 1. Special Branch Station/ File No. Date March 31, 1941.

SUBJECT: Exhibition of modern Japanese dramatic performances and moving pictures to be held at the Japanese Modern Science Library in Shanghai.

The Japanese Modern Science Library in Shanghai at No.149 Szechuen Road will hold an exhibition of Japanese dramatic performances and moving pictures in two rooms on the ground floor of the Library building between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. daily for a period of four days commencing April 9. Between 6 p.m. and 9 p.m. daily a cinema show and Kamishibai (paper picture dramatic plays) will be given at the same place.

The management of the Library desire to hold the exhibition for the purpose of giving the general public a better understanding of real Japanese dramatic and cinematographic art, thereby facilitating cultural interflow between Japan and China. Admission to the exhibition and the entertainment will be free.

When interviewed, Mr, Kamizaki, President of the Library stated that as the exhibition and the entertainment, which are not of a serious nature, are to be given inside the building and would be on a small scale, he would not particularly request the S.M.P. to take precautionary measures.

It is not yet known whether the cinema film to be used is of the ordinary inflamable commercial variety or of the 'safety' type.

A. C. (Special Branch).

主题：拟在上海日本现代科学图书馆举办日本现代戏剧表演及电影展览。

位于四川路149号的上海日本现代科学图书馆，将于4月9日起为期四天，每天上午9时至下午6时，在该图书馆大楼底层的两个房间内举办日本戏剧表演及电影展览。每天下午6时至9时，将在同一地点放映电影并表演“纸芝居”（Kamishibai，即画片剧）。

图书馆管理层表示，举办此次展览旨在让公众更好地了解真实的日本戏剧和电影艺术，从而促进中日文化交流。展览及娱乐活动均免费入场。

在接受问询时，该图书馆馆长神崎（Kamizaki，音译）先生表示，由于此次展览及娱乐活动性质并不严肃，且在室内举行，规模较小，因此他不特别要求上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）采取预防措施。

目前尚不清楚拟使用的电影胶片是普通的易燃商业胶片，还是“安全”型胶片。

A. C. （特别巡捕房）。

SUBJECT: Exhibition of modern Japanese dramatic performances and moving pictures to be held at the Japanese modern science library in Shanghai.

With reference to the attached translation of an article appearing in the March 25th issue of the "Tairiku Shimpo", I have to report that the exhibition will be held in the ground floor rooms of the Japanese Modern Science Library in Shanghai, located at No.149 Szechuen Road, between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. daily for a period of four days commencing April 9. Between 6 p.m. and 7 p.m. daily a cinema show will be given at the same place.

Articles to be shown at the exhibition have not yet arrived from Japan and the programme has not yet been drawn up. Upon the arrival of the exhibits from Japan, the management of the library will officially forward a letter to the S.M.P. requesting the necessary precautionary measures.

Admission to the exhibition and the entertainment will be free of charge.

MAINICHI :-

KOREAN SOCIETY TO BE MERGED WITH THE JAPANESE
RESIDENTS' CORPORATION

In conformity with the desire of
the Japanese Consulate-General, the Japanese Residents'
Corporation will take over the Korean Society. In this
connection, an ordinary meeting of the Corporation will
be held on March 25, at which a proposition to take over
the Korean Society will be made.
The Korean Society is granted by
the Government of Chosen a sum of Yen 10,000 every year
for the expenses of its kindergarten, Yen 6,000 by the
Japanese Foreign Office and Yen 3,000 by the Harada-
Sekizen-kai Association.
The property owned by the Korean
Society at present is valued at Yen 13,400, while the
Society has no deficit.

MAINICHI :-

EXHIBITION OF MODERN JAPANESE DRAMATIC PERFORMANCES
AND MOVING PICTURES TO BE HELD AT THE JAPANESE
MODERN SCIENCE LIBRARY IN SHANGHAI

With a view to enabling Chinese
people to have a better understanding of Japanese dramatic
performances and moving pictures, the Japanese Modern
Science Library in Shanghai will hold an exhibition of
modern Japanese dramatic performances and moving pictures
in its building on Szechuen Road for three days from March 9.
The articles to be exhibited will
be classified into dramatic performance section and moving
picture section.

《每日新闻》:-

朝鲜人协会将并入日本居留民团

遵照日本总领事馆的意愿，日本居留民团将接管朝鲜人协会。为此，居留民团将于3月25日举行常会，会上将提出接管朝鲜人协会的提案。

朝鲜人协会目前拥有的财产估值为13,400日元，且该协会无赤字。

Sir,

At 2.15p.m. 19-12-40, a telephone message was

Library of Japan to the effect that some anti-Japanese
slogans written by pencil were found on the gate post
of the above mentioned address.

Enquiries by C.D.S. 39 and D.P.S. Honda.

According to a Japanese named J. Kusuda (楠田卯之)
Chief of General Dept. of the library, at 12noon
19-12-40, he was leaving the premises for partaking of
his tiffin when he observed the slogans written on the
gate-post which had been decorated for the Exhibition
of Japanese Literature held since 14-12-40.

He explained that this might have been done between
12noon and 10a.m. this date when he had attended the
office and found nothing abnormal.

The slogans read as follows:-

1. Anti-Japanese Imperialism (打倒日本帝國主義)
2. Annihilate traitors (消滅一切漢奸)
3. Up hold Generalissimo Chiang Kai-Shek (擁護蔣委員長)
4. Resist to the end. (抗戰到底國策).

The slogans were erased by a coolie employed by the
library in accordance with the order by Police.

Subject... Central News Agency and Central China Daily News - to hold an
exhibition of travellers' photos.

Made by... D. I. Kao Yen Ken ...Forwarded by... D. I. Crawford

At 3 p.m. October 14, Chih Hung Sung
(吉鴻勝), a coolie of the Central China Daily
News, Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building, North
Honan Road, called at Police Headquarters and
requested permission to post copies of a poster
on the walls of houses in the Settlement. A specimen
is attached. The poster relates to an exhibition
of photos taken by travellers while in North China
and Hankow and is sponsored by the Central News
Agency, the Central China Daily News and the Modern
Scientific Library (Japanese). According to the
poster the exhibition will be open from 8 a.m. to
6 p.m. between October 14 and 21 in the Modern
Scientific Library, corner of Szechuen and Foochow
Roads.

On the instructions of D.I. Crawford, he was
instructed to inform the sponsors that permission
should be obtained first from the S.M.C. before
such posters can be posted. He promised to carry
out the instructions.

A visit has been paid to the exhibition, most
of the exhibits are of landscapes and there is
nothing of an objectionable nature.

D. C.(Special Branch).
D. I.

Incident during a cinema performance at Shanghai Japanese
Modern Science Library, 149 Szechuen Road.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

A responsible official of the Shanghai Japanese
Modern Science Library has been interviewed and requested
to avoid making unnecessary noise at future performances.

Residents of the Hamilton House have also been warned
by Inspector White.

Investigations revealed that some 800 persons attended
the performance on the evening of September 29 and that most
of these people were Chinese.

The performance was held in the compound at the rear of
the Museum and which is just below the East Wing of the
Hamilton House.

Talking pictures were shown and music played throughout
the performance, which started at 8 p.m. and finished
shortly after 10 p.m.

The compound is located between high buildings and the
noise of the talking machine must have been heard on the top
floors of the Hamilton House.

Complaints filed with the Police by residents of the
Hamilton House are justified and there can be no doubt about
it that those organising the performance must be aware of
this and the annoyance they were causing to others.

One resident of the Hamilton House informed the under-
signed that the noise was terrible and that he did not
consider it wise for the Japanese to hold such a performance
in view of the political tension.

The following complaints received from residents on
Sept. 29 substantiate the above:-

7.40 p.m.             FROM MISS GULSTON, 804 HAMILTON HOUSE
29-9-40.
                      Complaining re noise being caused by Japanese
                      conducting an open-air cinema performance in the
                      compound of premises situated next to and East of
                      Hamilton House for several consecutive nights.

7.50 p.m.             FROM MRS.C.FLETCHER, 809 HAMILTON HOUSE
29-9-40.
                      Reporting some Japanese conducting an open-
                      air cinema show in the compound adjoining Hamilton
                      House on the East side of Foochow Road for the 2nd
                      night, and so far as could be ascertained are going to
                      continue the show next night as well. The pictures
                      shown seem to be of purely propaganda character and
                      may have grave consequences if some Chinese attempts
                      to throw a grenade or something of the kind.

9.15 p.m.             FROM MISS GULSTON, 804 HAMILTON HOUSE
29-9-40.
                      Further to earlier complaint re noise caused
                      by open-air cinema show conducted by Japanese in
                      the compound adjoining Hamilton House at the East
                      repeating complaint.

Both parties were informed that the performance had been
sanctioned and that a police-officer would be sent to try and
stop the noise.

四川路149号上海日本现代科学图书馆电影放映期间发生的事件。
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

已约谈上海日本现代科学图书馆的一名负责官员，并要求其在未来的演出中避免制造不必要的噪音。

怀特（White）巡官也已警告汉密尔顿公寓的居民。

调查显示，9月29日晚约有800人观看了演出，其中大多数为中国人。

演出在博物馆后院的场地举行，该场地位于汉密尔顿公寓东翼的正下方。

演出从晚上8点开始，10点刚过结束，全程放映有声电影并播放音乐。

该场地位于高楼之间，扩音器的噪音必然会被汉密尔顿公寓顶层住户听到。

汉密尔顿公寓居民向警方提出的投诉是正当的，毫无疑问，组织演出者必然意识到这一点以及他们给他人造成的困扰。

汉密尔顿公寓的一位居民告知签署人，噪音极其可怕，并且鉴于政治紧张局势，他认为日本人举行此类演出是不明智的。

以下9月29日收到的居民投诉证实了上述情况：-

晚上7:40             来自汉密尔顿公寓804室 古尔斯顿（GULSTON）小姐
1940年9月29日。      投诉日本人连续数晚在紧邻汉密尔顿公寓东侧的物业院落内举行露天电影放映所造成的噪音。

晚上7:50             来自汉密尔顿公寓809室 C.弗莱彻（C.FLETCHER）夫人
1940年9月29日。      报告称一些日本人在福州路东侧紧邻汉密尔顿公寓的院落内进行第二晚的露天电影放映，据查他们明晚也将继续放映。放映的影片似乎纯属宣传性质，如果有中国人试图投掷手榴弹或类似物品，可能会产生严重后果。

晚上9:15             来自汉密尔顿公寓804室 古尔斯顿（GULSTON）小姐
1940年9月29日。      就早前关于日本人在汉密尔顿公寓东侧相邻院落举行露天电影放映造成噪音的投诉，再次提出投诉。

双方均被告知演出已获批准，并将派遣一名警员前去设法制止噪音。

- 2 -

The egg throwing incident occurred after 9 p.m.
and an examination of the spot revealed evidence
to indicate that several eggs had been thrown into
the compound from the Hamilton House or adjoining
buildings.
Mr. Cho Son Ki, who was interviewed, stated the
eggs were scattered amongst the audience quite near
to the projecting machine.

The sudden shock caused the audience to rise
from their seats and flee in panic to the exit gate.

Pandemonium reigned for a few minutes and at least
three Chinese are known to have sustained slight injuries
in addition to ten benches being broken.

Order was soon restored and the performance
continued, but the majority of the patrons had already
left.

A second incident occurred after the performance
when a medicine bottle was thrown at a Chinese coolie
who was clearing up the compound.

Mr. Cho Son Ki further stated that water was thrown
at him from the Hamilton House just before the performance
started.

The throwing of the eggs into the midst of the
audience was foolhardy act and might have had grave
results. There can be no excuse for this despite
the provocation.

Mr. and Mrs. Fletcher have been interviewed and
state that they know nothing regarding the egg throwing.
They kindly permitted an inspection of their apartment
which is located some considerable distance south of
the compound where the performance took place. It is
very much doubted if they could throw anything from
their apartment into the compound.

Mr. Fletcher stated that he did not think it wise
for the Police to permit such performance.

Efforts are being made to trace the owner of the
medicine bottle.

Further report will be submitted.

Certified true copy

J. Farrell

- 2 -

投掷鸡蛋事件发生在晚上9点之后，对现场的检查发现证据表明，有几个鸡蛋是从汉密尔顿公寓或邻近建筑物扔进院落的。

接受问询的赵孙基（Cho Son Ki，音译）先生表示，鸡蛋散落在观众中，离放映机很近。

突如其来的惊吓导致观众从座位上起身，惊慌失措地逃向出口大门。

现场混乱了几分钟，已知至少有三名中国人受轻伤，此外还有十条长凳被砸坏。

秩序很快恢复，演出继续进行，但大多数观众已经离开。

第二起事件发生在演出结束后，当时有人向一名正在清理院落的中国苦力投掷了一个药瓶。

赵孙基先生进一步表示，在演出开始前不久，有人从汉密尔顿公寓向他泼水。

向观众中间投掷鸡蛋是一种鲁莽的行为，可能会导致严重后果。尽管存在挑衅行为，但这不能成为借口。

已约谈弗莱彻（Fletcher）夫妇，他们表示对投掷鸡蛋一事一无所知。他们善意地允许检查其公寓，该公寓位于演出场地以南相当远的距离。非常令人怀疑他们是否能从公寓向院落内投掷任何物品。

弗莱彻先生表示，他认为警方允许此类演出是不明智的。

目前正在努力追查药瓶的主人。

将提交进一步报告。

核证无误副本

J. Farrell
----------------
JHS.

30th September 1940

The Secretariat,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Dear Sirs,

It was with great surprise that I learned from
the Officer-in-Charge, Charge Room, Central Police Station,
that permission had been granted to a Japanese concern
immediately next to the East side of Hamilton House to hold
an open air cinema. The hours, granted, from 8 O'clock to
10 might be considered reasonable but if could not have been
realized at the time permission was given that the cinema would
have been accompanied by the blaring noise of a loud speaker.

I strongly protest but hope for no comfort
of relief for yet perhaps another painful two hours.

During the past two years, building have been
allowed to hammer away in the vicinity. My only dread is
that this permission having been given one might be let in
for a disquieting winter, should other Japanese apply.

Your faithfully,

(signed) P.R. Gulston

敬启者：

当我从中央巡捕房值班室主管警官处得知，已批准紧邻汉密尔顿公寓东侧的一家日本机构举行露天电影放映时，我感到非常惊讶。获批的时间从8点到10点或许可以被认为是合理的，但在给予许可时，显然没有意识到电影放映会伴随着扩音器刺耳的噪音。

我强烈抗议，但不指望在接下来的两个小时痛苦中得到任何安慰或缓解。

此致

敬礼

TAIRIKU SHIMPO.

INCIDENT AT CULTURAL GATHERING HELD BY JAPANESE
LIBRARY ASSOCIATION.

Several Chinese were injured at a meeting of the Japan
Modern Science Library at 9.20 p.m. on Sept. 29, when an uniden-
tified person threw no less than 20 eggs from the floor, supposed
to be the sixth, of the Hamilton House at an audience of 800
attending the "Evening of movie and music showing Japanese cultural
development" which was held under the auspices of the Science
Library. As the audience mistook the eggs for bombs, a disturbance
was created and as a result several of them were injured. After
it was found that it was eggs that were thrown, the performance was
continued and at about 10 o'clock the meeting ended. Shortly after
that when coolies of the Library were cleaning the place a bottle
of medicine was thrown from an upper floor of the Hamilton House.
Fortunately no one was injured this time, but an official of the
Library reported the incident to the Central Police Station and
asked for a search for the culprit.

A formal protest will be made with the S.M.P. on the 30th.
An official of the Science Library told a representative of
the Tairiku Shimpo as follows:

"A policeman of the S.M.P. came to the meeting place during
the performance and said that a complaint was made by a foreigner
living in the Hamilton House. He explained that the gathering
was being held for three nights from 8 to 10 o'clock with the
permission of the Police. He understood the situation and left
the place, encouraging us. It was shortly after that policeman
left that eggs were thrown. The culprit may be the foreigner who
made a complaint to the Police. Attack on such a cultural gather-
ing is most deplorable. We hope that the Police will effectively
suppress such activities. As there is a label on the bottle of
medicine, the culprit will without fail be identified".

---
(Trans. by Y.H.)

《大陆新报》。

日本图书馆协会举办的文化集会事件。

9月29日晚9时20分，在日本现代科学图书馆的一次集会上，数名中国人受伤。当时，一名身份不明的人从汉密尔顿公寓（Hamilton House）的楼层（据信为六楼）向正在参加“电影与音乐欣赏之夜”（展示日本文化发展）的800名观众投掷了不少于20枚鸡蛋。该活动由科学图书馆主办。由于观众误将鸡蛋当作炸弹，现场发生骚乱，导致数人受伤。在发现投掷物为鸡蛋后，演出继续进行，会议于约10时结束。此后不久，当图书馆的苦力正在清理场地时，有人从汉密尔顿公寓的高层投下一瓶药水。幸运的是，此次无人受伤，但图书馆的一名官员已向中央捕房报告此事，并要求搜查肇事者。

将于30日向上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）提出正式抗议。
科学图书馆的一名官员向《大陆新报》记者陈述如下：

“警务处的一名警察在演出期间来到会场，称住在汉密尔顿公寓的一名外国人提出了投诉。他解释说，此次集会已获警方许可，将于每晚8时至10时举行，持续三晚。他了解了情况后便离开现场，并对我们表示鼓励。就在那名警察离开后不久，鸡蛋被投掷进来。肇事者可能是向警方投诉的那名外国人。对如此文化集会的攻击最令人遗憾。我们希望警方能有效制止此类活动。由于药水瓶上有标签，肇事者必定会被查明”。

---
（Y.H. 译）
